newsitem.title: USA: ANTHRAX CLAIMS AT LEAST 25 SOUTH DAKOTA CATTLE.
newsitem.headline: ANTHRAX CLAIMS AT LEAST 25 SOUTH DAKOTA CATTLE.

text.p: Three confirmed cases of anthrax over the past two weeks have claimed the lives of at least 25 cattle in South Dakota, the state's veterinarian said Friday.
Sam Holland, South Dakota state veterinarian, said all three anthrax outbreaks have occurred within a five- or six-mile area in the southeast part of the state.
Holland said the disease was not unusual in the U.S. Plains, where anthrax spores can live in soil indefinitely.
"Our state, like most Great Plains states, is endemic for anthrax," Holland said.
The most recent outbreak was in Davison County, where the disease killed three head of cattle. Last week, at least 22 cows died from anthrax in Hutchinson County.

Holland said the state had quarantined the affected farms and had ensured that the animal carcasses were being disposed of properly. Animals in the affected herds were also being vaccinated against the disease.
"This is no big alarm or panic. We do quarantine and make sure that the carcasses are properly disposed of so as to... prevent more cases down the road," Holland said.
Anthrax is a bacterial disease that causes rapid death in cattle and sheep.

While it generally does not affect humans, at least two Ukrainians died and 29 more were infected by anthrax in May in an outbreak that local media blamed on diseased meat that was given to workers instead of wages.
